title: A Bayes Classifier, by Hand
tagline: Two Gaussians and a prior — build the optimal classifier and watch the decision boundary move
summary: Two class-conditional Gaussians, one prior slider, and a draggable test point. Multiply likelihood by prior, normalize, and you have the posterior p(Y=1|x) — the provably optimal classifier. Drag the test point to read its predicted class and posterior; slide the prior and watch the decision boundary slide with it. This is the machinery underneath logistic regression, Gaussian discriminant analysis, and naive Bayes.
highlights: See two class-conditional Gaussians and the posterior p(Y=1|x) that Bayes' rule builds from them.
The decision boundary appears exactly where the posterior crosses 0.5 — drag the sliders and it moves live.
Lower the prior on class 1 and watch the boundary shift toward class 1's territory, shrinking its region.
Unequal variances bend the boundary into two crossing points — a peek at quadratic discriminant analysis.
Drag a test point to read its predicted class and posterior probability, the optimal decision at every location.
